name: Wyre Forest

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households). The council has consulted (2025 to 2026) on an Article 4 Direction so that new small HMOs in Kidderminster would need planning permission.

neighbourhoods.name: Offmore and Comberton

neighbourhoods.name: Stourport-on-Severn

neighbourhoods.name: Bewdley

neighbourhoods.name: Blakedown and Cookley

neighbourhoods.name: Wolverley and Franche

neighbourhoods.housing: Cottages, smallholdings and bungalows in the Wyre Forest woodland.

housing: Wyre Forest is made up of the former carpet town of Kidderminster, the canal town of Stourport-on-Severn and the riverside town of Bewdley, with villages and woodland around them. Kidderminster has many Victorian terraces and converted mill buildings, and HMOs are concentrated there. Large interwar and post-war estates surround the town, and park homes and holiday caravans are common around Stourport. Bewdley and Stourport sit on the Severn, which floods regularly.
checkinTips: Riverside homes in Bewdley and Stourport-on-Severn: photograph flood defences, airbricks, flood doors and any watermarks.
Victorian terraces in Kidderminster: photograph back yards, damp in rear kitchens and older windows.
Converted carpet mill and factory flats: note fobs, ventilation, shared areas and parking.
Park homes around Stourport: record the pitch, skirting, steps, sheds and the site rules that apply.
Listed Georgian homes in Bewdley: record original features carefully, as repairs need consent.
Woodland homes near Far Forest: check gutters, roofs and trees close to the house, and note any oil tank or septic tank.
tenantHelp: Wyre Forest District Council's Private Sector Housing team investigates disrepair and unsafe conditions in private rented homes and licenses HMOs.
